value.title: Product-envelope factorization and receiver-skew reduction
value.summary: A conditional Csiszár sum identity factors the receiver-information difference across product-channel coordinates, including correlated input laws and joint envelope auxiliaries. Product posterior ensembles give the reverse inequality. An involutive receiver-exchanging input relabeling then identifies the two relaxed rows at invariant priors and extends the equality to finite receiver-skew products.

value.title: Half-skew BSSC posterior-contact evaluation
value.summary: At the invariant binary input prior, the half-skew BSSC receiver informations equal h_2(1/4)-1/2. The sharp posterior-support inequality and the posterior mixture with masses 5/8 at q=4/5 and 3/8 at q=0 give envelope value h_2(1/4)-3/4, yielding the one-letter scalar 2h_2(1/4)-5/4 bits.

value.title: High-precision half-skew BSSC specialization audit
value.summary: A standard-library high-precision script checks the half-skew channel relabeling identities, the attaining posterior mixture, the support-contact equality, and the numerical value of 2h_2(1/4)-5/4. It corroborates the exact specialization but does not replace the analytic product and symmetry proof.

value.title: Tensorization theorem for separately relaxed UV scalars
value.summary: For finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channels, the averaged separately relaxed UV sum-rate scalar is exactly additive under products. For receiver-skew channels the branchwise scalar equals the averaged scalar, and both are additive on every finite receiver-skew product. Hence, for the half-skew BSSC P and every n≥1, both scalars on P^×n equal n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) bits. This does not assert tensorization of the full UV region, a common joint-(U,V) optimization, the GK functional, or capacity.

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted theorem directly advances the existing objective of determining tensorization and receiver-skew equality for separately relaxed scalar UV converse functionals.
